items.text: Following President Hage Geingob’s passing, Nangolo Mbumba assumed the role of interim president of Namibia. Mbumba stated he wouldn’t run in the upcoming elections, adhering to his desire to serve as a school principal. This decision paves the way for Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah to run, potentially making her Namibia’s first female president. Mbumba’s humility contrasts with the typical power retention seen among African leaders. Namibia aims to lead in green energy initiatives, exemplified by its endeavors in hydrogen and minerals for clean energy. Geingob’s legacy includes efforts to combat racial inequalities and promote green economy leadership, positioning Namibia as a global example of sustainability. Difficult words: adhere (to believe in and follow the practices of), retention (the continued possession, use, or control of something), exemplified (shown as an example). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

After President Hage Geingob’s death, Nangolo Mbumba became Namibia’s interim president. Mbumba said that he wouldn’t run in the elections, because he wished to be a school principal. This decision allows Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah to run, which could make her Namibia’s first female president. Mbumba’s choice breaks from the norm of African leaders who usually want to stay in power as long as possible. Namibia wants to be a leader in green energy and invest in hydrogen and minerals. This makes the country more special than any other African state. Difficult words: interim (for a limited period), norm (how things usually are), hydrogen (a gas with no color or smell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Namibia’s leader Hage Geingob dies. Nangolo Mbumba takes over. But only for a short time. Mbumba will not take part in the next election . He wants to be a boss in school. This is a chance for Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah. She can become the first woman president. Geingob works to make Namibia better. He fights racism and other important problems. Nobody knows what will happen now. But the country wants to be the leader in green energy and make things cleaner. Namibia wants to be the best African country in green energy. Difficult words: election (when people choose a person for a job in politics), racism (when someone does not like someone else because he or she has a different skin color), green energy (making energy in a way which does not hurt the planet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two teenagers Scarlett Jenkinson and Eddie Ratcliffe have been sentenced to life in prison for the exceptionally brutal murder of Brianna Ghey, a 16-year-old British transgender girl, in February last year. The judge revealed the crime was partly motivated by Brianna’s transgender identity. Jenkinson, described as the driving force, received a minimum sentence of 22 years, and Ratcliffe, a former kickboxer, received 20 years. The murder was meticulously planned, with Jenkinson expressing a desire to kill and creating a kill list. The judge warned that the pair might never be released if they remain a danger. The court heard disturbing details of the murder, including 28 stab wounds, and Jenkinson’s admission to wanting parts of Brianna’s body as a token . Difficult words: meticulously (very carefully and precisely), token (a symbol or sign). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Manchester court sentenced Scarlett Jenkinson and Eddie Ratcliffe, both 16, to life in prison. One year ago, they brutally killed Brianna Ghey, a transgender girl. Jenkinson received a minimum of 22 years, while Ratcliffe, a former kickboxer, got 20 years. The crime was partly motivated by Brianna’s transgender identity. The court revealed disturbing details, including 28 stab wounds. Jenkinson was obsessed with serial killers and she admitted that she wanted parts of Brianna’s body as a token . The judge warned that the pair might never get out of prison if they remain a danger. Difficult words: transgender (a person who feels to be a different identity than the sex they were born with), obsessed (when your mind is full of something and you can’t stop thinking about it), token (a symbol or sign). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One year ago, two British teenagers, Scarlett Jenkinson, and Eddie Ratcliffe, kill Brianna Ghey. They kill her in a park. The killing is very brutal . Brianna Ghey is a 16-year-old transgender girl. The judge says that they hurt Brianna a lot because of that. Scarlett will stay in prison for at least 22 years, and Eddie for 20 years. The judge warns that they may never leave if they are still dangerous. Scarlett plans the murder. She just wants to kill. She has a list of people to kill. She is interested in serial killers . Scarlett also wants to keep parts of Brianna’s body. The judge says that this is a terrible crime. Difficult words: brutal (cruel and without feelings), serial killer (a person who kills more people in separate incidents), terrible (very bad). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A ship carrying 16,000 sheep and cows, initially bound for Israel, turned back from the Red Sea due to the risk of attacks by Yemen’s Houthi militia. Stranded in an Australian port due to biosecurity rules during a heatwave, the exporter, Israeli firm Bassem Dabbah, seeks permission to offload some animals into quarantine. Another vessel, the Jawan, carrying around 60,000 animals, is en route to Jordan but has a contingency plan to unload in the Gulf if Red Sea entry is denied. The MV Bahijah, managed by Korkyra Shipping, faces uncertainty as Australian officials consider the exporter’s request. Animal rights concerns and political pressure to ban live sheep exports persist as the situation unfolds. Difficult words: biosecurity (measures to protect against the spread of harmful organisms), en route (on the way or in transit), contingency (a plan for an unexpected event). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A ship with 16,000 sheep and cows, going to Israel, turned back due to dangers from Yemen. Now, the ship is in an Australian port during a heatwave, and the exporter wants to unload some animals. Another ship, the Jawan, is heading to Jordan with 60,000 animals. If it can’t go through the Red Sea, it might unload in the Gulf. Australia’s agriculture ministry is deciding about the stranded ship. Some people worry about the animals’ treatment and want to ban live sheep exports. Australia’s live export industry faces challenges, with over half a million sheep and cattle sent overseas last year. Difficult words: exporter (a person or company which sends things to another country for sale), stranded (unable to leave a place because of a problem with transport, money, and to son), treatment (how someone behaves towards someone or something else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big ship with 16,000 sheep and cows is going to Israel. But it must turn back. It is too dangerous. Yemen’s Houthis may attack the ship. Now, the ship is stuck in Australia because of the hot weather. The people who send the animals want to unload some of them. Another ship with 60,000 animals is going to Jordan. If it cannot go through the Red Sea, it may stop in the Gulf. Australian officials must decide what to do with the first ship. Some people are worried. Animals suffer on the ship. Millions of animals travel by ships around the world. Difficult words: stuck (when you are in a place and cannot move or leave), unload (to take things off a ship, vehicle, and so on), suffer (to go through something bad or unpleasant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Madelein Månsson, a 79-year-old Swede, defies age stereotypes by becoming a DJ for the 50 and up crowd at her disco. A former model and fitness coach, her love for music led her to create a space where people her age can dance without feeling out of place. She opens her disco at 6 pm, allowing guests to warm up with a drink before hitting the dance floor for four hours straight. Madelein encourages them to embrace the joy of dancing, ensuring they go home with 20,000 steps on their pedometers . Her positive attitude shines through, inspiring others to step out of their comfort zones. This sprightly senior, who faced adversity after her husband’s passing, now finds solace and purpose in spreading happiness through music. Difficult words: pedometer (a device that counts the number of steps a person takes), sprightly (lively, full of energy), adversity (a difficult or unpleasant situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Madelein Månsson is a 79-year-old Swede who loves music and dancing. And surprisingly, she is a DJ, too! She was not able to find a suitable place to dance, therefore, she became a DJ and opened her disco for people aged 50 and above. The disco starts at 6 pm, and it allows guests to dance for four hours straight. Madelein encourages everyone to enjoy the music and have fun. Even after facing challenges, like her husband’s passing , she remains positive and continues DJing. Her story teaches us to try new things and find joy in music, regardless of our age. Difficult words: encourage (to inspire or motivate), passing (when someone dies), regardless (without the influence of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Madelein Månsson is 79 years old. She likes music and dancing. She is the oldest DJ in Sweden. Madelein becomes a DJ because she cannot find a place to dance. She makes a disco for people who are over 50 years old. The disco starts at 6 pm. People can dance for four hours. Madelein says that people need to have fun. Madelein’s husband dies. It is a difficult time for her. But she stays positive . She is still a DJ. Her story teaches us to try new things and have joy in music. No matter how old we are. Difficult words: positive (thinking good things, not sad), joy (when you feel happy), no matter (when something is not a problem or important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The eurozone’s economy struggled to grow last year, avoiding a recession by a narrow margin, in contrast to the global economic expansion. Germany, a key player in the euro area, faced an industrial downturn , impacting the entire region. Germany’s economic contraction of 0.3% in Q4 2023 contributed to the eurozone’s stagnation , marking the sixth consecutive quarter of minimal growth. Economists predict a slow recovery, with household consumption expected to drive growth as energy prices stabilize and inflation subsides. However, the International Monetary Fund downgraded its growth forecast for the euro area to 0.9% in 2024. In contrast, the United States experienced significant growth, defying predictions of a recession. The eurozone’s economic challenges are compounded by strikes and protests over inflation, with uncertainties lingering into 2025. Difficult words: downturn (a decline), stagnation (a lack of growth or development), defy (to openly resist or refuse to obey). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The eurozone, a group of 20 countries, had a hard time growing its economy last year. It almost went into a recession . Germany is a significant contributor to the euro area, but it had big problems last year. This caused the whole area to not grow much. Experts say that it is because of problems in Germany’s business and trade with other countries. The United States, another big economy, did much better. While both areas faced higher prices, the US grew by 2.5%, while the eurozone only managed around 0.5%. There were also strikes and protests about high prices, and experts think things might not get much better until 2025. Difficult words: recession (a period when the economy is not growing), contributor (someone who takes part in something and has an impact on it), strike (when workers protest). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

2023 is a tough time for some countries in Europe. Some businesses do not do as well as they wish. They almost go into a recession . One of the big countries is Germany. When Germany has troubles, it has an impact on other countries, too. But in the United States, things are much better. Businesses do well. Many countries have trouble with high. People are unhappy. They protest . Experts say the European countries may not get much better until 2025. It takes time before some things change. Difficult words: tough (hard, difficult), recession (a time when the economy is not growing), protest (to show that you are not happy about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK government is set to ban disposable vapes to combat the rising youth vaping trend. This initiative, aimed at protecting children’s health, also includes measures to prevent marketing vapes to youngsters and curb underage sales. Although it’s already illegal to sell vapes to those under 18, disposable vapes, with their vibrant packaging, contribute significantly to the surge in youth vaping. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak assures access to alternatives for adult smokers trying to quit. Despite the UK Vaping Industry Association’s concerns about potential black market growth, the government emphasizes the need to address the alarming increase in youth vaping. The proposal aligns with a broader effort to create a smoke-free generation, with potential implementation in 2025. Difficult words: curb (to restrain or keep in check), vibrant (bright or exciting). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UK government plans to ban disposable vapes . The increasing number of young people taking up vaping is worrying. The plan is to stop vape marketing to children and underage sales. It is already illegal to sell vapes to those under 18, but disposable vapes play an important role in the rise of vaping among children. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak assures that adult smokers who look for alternatives to cigarettes will still be able to buy vape. The UK Vaping Industry Association is against the plan, because it may lead to illegal sale of vape. Officials say that the ban could start in early 2025. Difficult words: disposable (something you use once and then throw it away), vape (a type of e-cigarette), alternative (another possibility or thing you can choose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Vape is a type of e-cigarette. Many children in the UK use it. The UK government plans to stop this. It is now illegal to sell vapes to people under 18. But many children buy it anyway. The packaging has bright colors. Children like it. They do not think that vaping is dangerous. The new rules want to stop marketing vapes to children. Children under 18 will not have the chance to buy vape. Many adults use vape, too. They often do it when they want to stop smoking cigarettes. The ban may start in 2025. Difficult words: illegal (against the rules), marketing (a business activity which makes people buy something), ban (to officially stop something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed stunning images of 19 spiral galaxies, shedding light on star formation, galactic structure, and evolution. Shared by the Physics at High Angular resolution in Nearby GalaxieS (PHANGS) project, these images offer detailed insights into about 100,000 star clusters and millions, if not billions, of individual stars. Notable galaxies include NGC5068, around 15 million light-years away, and NGC1365, about 60 million light-years distant. The telescope was launched in 2021and it observes mainly in the infrared, providing a unique perspective on the early universe. University of Oxford astronomer Thomas Williams notes that these images are crucial for understanding the initial stages of star formation, a phase previously obscured from view. The observations reveal the structure of dust and gas clouds in unprecedented detail, allowing scientists to comprehend the intricate cycle of star formation and feedback. Difficult words: obscured (kept from being seen), comprehend (to understand), intricate (very complicated or detailed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The James Webb Space Telescope took remarkable images of 19 spiral galaxies. These images help scientists understand how stars are born and how galaxies form. These pictures show galaxies like NGC5068, which is 15 million light-years away, and NGC1365, 60 million light-years away. Scientists launched the telescope in 2021. It observes mainly in the infrared , which means that it can see through dust and study stars behind it. Astronomer Thomas Williams emphasized that the images helped understand early star formation. The images also show detailed structures of dust and gas clouds, which help our understanding of the star formation cycle . Difficult words: remarkable (amazing), infrared (set of colors at the end of the spectrum which people can’t see), cycle (a series of events which repeat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope starts taking pictures of the universe . Recently, it takes amazing pictures of 19 spiral galaxies. These pictures help us learn how stars are born. We know more about how galaxies evolve . The telescope mainly uses infrared light. People cannot see this light. This light can see through dust and study stars behind it. The galaxies in the pictures are quite far away. The NGC5068 galaxy is about 15 million light years from us. These images are special. They show many new details about stars. They also tell us more about dust and gas clouds. This is where new stars are born. Difficult words: universe (all space around us and everything what is in it, like stars, planets, and so on), galaxy (a system of stars, gas, and dust), evolve (to change over time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman in northern California faced a harrowing 14-hour ordeal after her pickup truck overturned in a swollen creek following heavy rain. The California Highway Patrol Air Operations used a helicopter to rescue her from the rushing waters. Dramatic footage showed a technician using a harness to lift her from the vehicle to safety. Despite spending the night atop the overturned truck, she sustained only minor injuries. The rescue involved multiple emergency agencies, including the highway patrol and local fire department. Recent rainfall led to unexpected high water levels in the Del Valle creek, causing the woman’s predicament . Remarkably, her decision to climb on top of the car is credited with saving her life, and she was airlifted to a hospital for treatment. Difficult words: harrowing (extremely distressing), ordeal (a very unpleasant and prolonged experience), predicament (a difficult or dangerous situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In northern California, a woman faced a dangerous 15-hour situation after her pickup truck overturned in a river during heavy rain. A helicopter team from the California Highway Patrol Air Operations started a daring rescue. They lifted the woman from the rushing waters using a harness . The woman wanted to cross Del Valle Creek , about 35 miles east of San Francisco, but she got stuck. She spent the night on top of her car, which probably saved her life. She survived with minor injuries. A similar incident took place in 2012 on the same creek. Difficult words: daring (bold and brave), harness (a piece of equipment which you fit under your arms or around the body to keep safe or in place), creek (a stream). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In northern California, a woman has a scary time. Her truck overturns in a big creek . It happens because it rains very much. She wants to cross the river. But there is too much water. The water is fast. The woman spends the night on top of the truck. She gets stuck for almost 15 hours. Someone camping nearby sees her the next morning. They call for help. A special helicopter team comes to help. The helicopter lifts her from the truck. The woman goes to the hospital with small injuries . This rescue is similar to one which happens in the same place in 2012. Difficult words: creek (a small river), stuck (not able to move or leave a place), injury (when you are hurt). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The world’s largest cruise ship Icon of the Seas is embarking on its inaugural voyage, using liquefied natural gas (LNG) as its fuel source. While LNG is cleaner than traditional marine fuel, environmental concerns arise regarding potential methane emissions. The ship, with a capacity for 8,000 passengers across 20 decks, symbolizes the growing popularity of cruises. However, experts warn that the use of LNG might result in harmful methane leakage during the combustion process, known as methane slip. The International Council on Clean Transportation estimates that LNG emits over 120% more greenhouse gas emissions than marine gas oil. Methane’s short-term harmful effects and its potency , being 80 times worse than carbon dioxide over 20 years, raise climate concerns. Despite Royal Caribbean’s claim of exceeding emissions efficiency standards, the environmental impact of LNG-powered cruise ships prompts calls for further scrutiny and research. Difficult words: inaugural (first), combustion (the process of burning something), potency (strength or power), scrutiny (careful examination). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The world’s largest cruise ship Icon of the Seas is ready for its first journey. It uses liquefied natural gas (LNG). LNG is cleaner than the fuel which ships normally use, but some experts worry about methane emissions. The ship has a capacity for 8,000 passengers and 20 decks. Such cruises are becoming more popular. The International Council on Clean Transportation says that LNG may produce over 120% more greenhouse gas emissions than usual fuel. Royal Caribbean claims that the ship will produce fewer emissions than usual, but environmental groups ask for careful examination and research into the impact of LNG-fueled cruise ships. Difficult words: liquefied (turned into liquid), fuel (a material which people use to produce heat or power), methane (a gas with no smell or color). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A very big cruise ship is starting its first trip. But some people are worried. The ship uses a special fuel . It is called liquefied natural gas or LNG. It is cleaner than the fuel which ships normally use. But when you burn it, you produce methane. Methane is a gas with no smell and color. It is not good for the air. It can make the Earth warmer quickly. The ship can have 8,000 passengers at one time. Many people like cruises nowadays. Some experts say that LNG is worse than the usual fuel. The ship’s company says that it is better. People are watching the situation. Many new ships will probably use LNG. Difficult words: cruise ship (a large ship which carries people on trips for fun), fuel (a material which people burn to get heat or power), liquefied (when people turn gas into liquid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alabama executed Kenneth Smith, a death row inmate , using nitrogen gas, an untested method challenged by his lawyers as cruel and unusual punishment. Smith’s death, intended to be humane, took 22 minutes, during which he appeared to struggle violently. Eyewitnesses described Smith writhing, convulsing , and gasping for air. The White House expressed deep concern over the execution, questioning its consistency with American values. Smith’s lawyers argued that the untried procedure violated constitutional protections against cruelty, especially since Smith had survived a previous failed execution attempt. The new method involved a respirator mask and pure nitrogen, causing fatal oxygen deprivation. Despite international criticism and opposition from UN experts, Alabama proceeded with the execution, raising concerns about the potential adoption of nitrogen hypoxia in other states. Difficult words: death row inmate (a prisoner who has been sentenced to death), convulse (to experience involuntary muscle contractions), nitrogen hypoxia (a method that causes fatal oxygen deprivation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Alabama executed Kenneth Smith using nitrogen gas. It was a new method which was not tested before. The procedure lasted 22 minutes, during which Smith visibly struggled for air. The procedure involved a mask and pure nitrogen. There was no oxygen, but the man tried to breathe for some time. The White House expressed deep concern about whether this method was still okay and in line with American values. Smith’s lawyers argued that the method was cruel . Despite international criticism, Alabama proceeded with the execution. Some people worry that other US states could use this method in the future, too. Difficult words: struggle (to fight to get free or get something), in line (in agreement), cruel (something what causes pain or makes someone suffer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Alabama executes Kenneth Smith. They use nitrogen gas. It is a new thing. It never happens before. The new way uses a mask. The man gets only nitrogen through the mask. He stops breathing. Some people do not like it. Smith has a hard time during the execution . It lasts 22 minutes. The White House is worried about it. Many people and countries do not agree with this way of execution. They say that it is too long and too painful . Alabama does it anyway. People think that other US states may do the same in the future, too. Difficult words: execute (to kill a person who does something very bad), execution (killing a person who does something very bad), painful (when something hurts very much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The final Davos panel of 2024 revealed an uneasy equilibrium in the world, where a more positive economic backdrop is overshadowed by numerous geopolitical risks. Despite prospects of easing inflation and a global trade upswing , European Central Bank Chief Christine Lagarde highlighted the shift toward ‘ normalization ’ but cautioned against viewing it as true normality. The optimism at Davos, especially among business leaders, raised concerns for some observers who recall that Davos consensus has historically been inaccurate. Business leaders expressed optimism about increased sales and consumer demand, prompting questions about the need for six rate cuts in the US. Geopolitical uncertainties and a lack of market reaction to such risks were noted, leading to a focus on potential tail risks like unexpected rate cuts or heightened geopolitical tensions. Difficult words: equilibrium (a balanced state), upswing (an upward trend), normalization (returning to a normal state), consensus (a general agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The final Davos panel in 2024 revealed a world in an uncertain balance. There are positive economic news but geopolitical risks at the same time. Christine Lagarde, who leads the European Central Bank, said that while inflation is going down and global trade is going up, it doesn’t mean everything is normal. Business leaders are optimistic about increased sales and consumer demand, but what experts previously agreed on didn’t always work well. Markets don’t respond to geopolitical troubles, which is something what many see as dangerous. These are, for example, unexpected rate cuts or world conflicts. Difficult words: geopolitical (connected with political activity and geography of a country or area), inflation (the price of money), rate cut (when a central bank reduces its main interest rate). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The final Davos meeting in 2024 talks about the economic situation in the world. And the situation is not very sure. Some things in the economy look good. But there are also big problems. Some countries are not friendly to each other. Christine Lagarde leads the European Central Bank. She says that while inflation is going down and global trade is going up. But it does not mean that everything is normal. Business leaders are happy about selling more things. But some people worry because, in the past, Davos is not always right. They are also not sure why the market is not reacting to problems between countries. So, there may be more problems in the future which nobody expects now. Difficult words: economic (relating to business or money), inflation (the price of money), expect (to think that something will happen in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has intensified its scrutiny of Boeing by recommending inspections on Boeing 737-900ER jets. This comes after reports of unspecified bolt issues with door plugs. The move follows a mid-air panel blowout on an Alaska Airlines MAX 9 jet, prompting heightened regulatory attention on Boeing. The FAA advises airlines to inspect mid-exit door plugs on 737-900ER planes, with findings of bolt issues noted during maintenance inspections. Although the 737-900ER is an older model, it shares an optional door plug design with the newer 737 MAX 9. Boeing, facing quality control concerns, has grounded 171 MAX 9 planes, and the FAA recommends prompt inspections to ensure safety. Difficult words: scrutiny (careful examination), blowout (an occasion when a tire on a vehicle or a device burst). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The FAA asked Boeing for careful examination and inspection of Boeing 737-900ER jets. There were reports of problems with door bolts. This increased attention follows a mid-air panel accident on an Alaska Airlines MAX 9 jet, which led to a grounding of 171 MAX 9 planes. The FAA advises airlines to inspect 737-900ER mid-exit door plugs because there were problems during maintenance inspections . Although it is an older model, the 737-900ER has the same door plug design as the grounded MAX 9. Boeing is taking the situation seriously and the company asked for an independent advisor. At the same time, Boeing will support the FAA’s actions. Difficult words: attention (notice), grounding (keeping a plane on the ground), maintenance inspection (checking a piece of equipment or machine). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The FAA is looking more closely at Boeing. It suggests checks on Boeing 737-900ER. There are bolt troubles with door plugs . These worries come after a problem with an Alaska Airlines MAX 9 jet. An accident happens when the plane is in the air. Boeing stops 171 MAX 9 planes. The FAA advises airlines to check door plugs. Inspectors find problems with some planes. The 737-900ER is an older model. But it has a similar design to the MAX 9. Boeing must explain many things. People worry about safety. The FAA says that safety is the most important thing in its inspections . Difficult words: bolt (a bar that holds a door or window closed), door plug (a special type of door, usual in planes), inspection (check or examination). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a new Hindu temple in Ayodhya, replacing a mosque demolished by Hindu radicals over three decades ago. The temple holds deep religious significance, symbolizing Lord Ram’s return to his supposed birthplace. Modi emphasized the fulfillment of a long-cherished dream and he played a central role in the consecration ceremony, marked by rituals and offerings. The event drew 8,000 guests and numerous pilgrims, while Ayodhya underwent a significant government-funded transformation. Some view it as a divine moment, while others criticize it as a political gimmick ahead of upcoming elections. The construction’s association with Hindu nationalism raises concerns about India’s secular identity. The temple’s completion is expected next year. The historical disputes over the Ayodhya site date back a century, marked by the 1992 mosque demolition and subsequent legal battles. Difficult words: consecration (making something sacred), gimmick (a trick or scheme often used to attract attention or promote something), secular (a system that’s not related to religious matters or doesn’t have a religious basis). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently inaugurated a new Hindu temple in Ayodhya. The temple replaced a mosque demolished 30 years ago. The ceremony was full of rituals and offerings , and many people came to see it. Many consider it an important religious moment. It symbolizes Lord Ram’s return for them. But critics say that Modi planned the event carefully because of the upcoming elections. Workers should complete the temple next year. Historical disputes over Ayodhya started over a century ago, and they escalated in 1992 with the mosque’s destruction. The top court said that it was illegal in 2019 but awarded the land to Hindus. The event brings many emotions, some people celebrate but for others, it brings back bad memories. Difficult words: inaugurate (to officially start or open something), offering (a gift to a god), dispute (an argument or fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Narendra Modi is the leader of India’s government. He opens a new Hindu temple in Ayodhya. The temple is on the site of a mosque . But people destroy the mosque 30 years ago. Many see opening the temple as an important moment. But others say that it is only about politics. There will be elections in India. The temple will be ready next year. Fights over Ayodhya start a hundred years ago. They become very serious in 1992. It is the last year of the mosque. In 2019, the top court says that destroying the mosque is against the law. But Hindus get the land. Some people are happy that there is a temple now. For others, it brings back bad things from the past. Difficult words: temple (a building important for people who believe in a god), mosque (a building important for Muslims), elections (when people choose a person for a job in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Doomsday Clock remains at 90 seconds to global catastrophe, according to the Bulletin of Atomic Scientists. Persistent global instability is attributed to factors such as Russia’s ongoing war in Ukraine, Israel’s actions following an Oct. 7 attack, Middle East proxy battles , stalled nuclear arms control talks, insufficient progress on climate change, and increasing risks associated with artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. The Board of Atomic Scientists emphasizes that the situation is not improving compared to the previous year. The potential for the United States being drawn into a war involving Israel and other Middle Eastern countries, climate change, record temperatures, and challenges posed by artificial intelligence are key concerns. The Board urges global leaders to take more decisive actions to address these threats. Difficult words: persistent (ongoing), proxy battle (an indirect conflict fought by third parties), stalled (without any progress). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Doomsday Clock remains at 90 seconds to global catastrophe . It is the closest point to midnight ever. The Bulletin of Atomic Scientists explains the main reasons why our planet is so close to a catastrophe. These are global instability due to Russia’s war in Ukraine, war in Gaza, Middle East conflicts, little progress in talks about nuclear weapons, little progress in climate change, and risks from artificial intelligence. The Board said that the situation didn’t get any better since last year. Scientists worry the United States will take part in a Middle East war, world temperatures will rise, and artificial intelligence will become dangerous. They ask world leaders to deal with these problems quickly. Difficult words: catastrophe (an event which hurts many people and causes big damage), instability (the situation when things are not stable or sure), progress (when things are getting better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
